clips.title: API Design Backward and Forward Compatible APIs
clips.why: A small API grows from version 1.0 to 1.1, and you see which changes old clients survive.
look: Version 1.0 and the client written against it.
What adding a feature in 1.1 does to that old client.
What backward compatible means: the old client keeps working with the new API.
clips.after: Customers' SDK versions are those old clients; the smoke test runs one of them against every pull request.

clips.title: API Design Backward and Forward Compatible APIs
clips.why: A breaking change, and the expand and contract way to make it without breaking anyone.
look: Why the change in version 1.2 breaks existing clients.
Expand: support the old and the new shape at the same time.
Contract: remove the old shape only when nobody needs it.
clips.after: The lab's to_internal_value is the expand step for the workgroup rename, and the smoke test proves it for SDK 1.0.

clips.title: What is Semantic Versioning?
clips.why: How version numbers promise compatibility, and why a promise is not enough: users depend on behaviour you never documented.
look: Major, minor and patch, and what each one promises.
Hyrum's law: with enough users, every observable behaviour is depended on by someone.
Why that makes testing the real old client more reliable than reading the changelog.
clips.after: A schema diff checks the promise; running the published SDK checks the behaviour customers actually rely on.

practice.q: Complete the command that runs the smoke test against the released wheel, for this command only.
practice.hint: A uv run flag that adds a package temporarily.
practice.why: --with installs the package into a temporary environment for this run, without making it a dependency of the project.

practice.q: Without transaction=True, the smoke test's created project is not found by the SDK. Why?

options.why: It is a full Django server; POST works.

options.text: The server thread uses its own database connection and cannot see rows the test has not committed.
options.why: transaction=True commits the rows and cleans the tables afterwards, so the server sees what the test wrote.

options.text: The SDK caches the old list of projects.
options.why: The SDK in the lab caches nothing; the server simply cannot see uncommitted rows.

practice.q: fcp's cloud project sets exclude-newer = "7 days". Yesterday the SDK team released a new version. What happens in the smoke step if nobody overrides it?

options.text: uv ignores the new release, so the step tests last week's SDK or fails to resolve the version.
options.why: exclude-newer also applies to --with, so the step must override it to test yesterday's release.

options.text: uv installs the newest release anyway, because --with ignores settings.
options.why: It does not; the project's setting applies to the extra package too.
Skipping happens only when no SDK is installed at all.

practice.q: Put a safe field rename in order.
items: The API accepts both the old and the new field name
The smoke test passes against the oldest supported SDK and the latest
A new SDK release sends the new name
Customers upgrade over the following months
When no supported SDK sends the old name, a later pull request removes it
practice.why: Expand, release, wait, contract: at every moment every supported SDK version works.

practice.q: Which change does oasdiff (comparing OpenAPI documents) miss, but the smoke test with the real SDK catches?

options.text: A required request field that was removed from the schema.
options.why: oasdiff sees that in the documents; it is a classic schema break.

options.text: The API now returns the list of projects in a different order, and the SDK's find_project takes the first one.
options.why: Order is behaviour, not schema. Only running the real client shows that it now picks the wrong project.
Adding an endpoint breaks nobody, and both checks stay green.
